questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of the .git directory?
options: The .git directory (or Git directory in some layouts) stores repository metadata, references, configuration and objects. Treat it as managed internal state and use Git commands instead of editing its files directly.
Git automatically backs up every file, including ignored and untracked files, to a remote.
The operation grants every contributor write access to the hosted repository.
questions.answer_key: The .git directory (or Git directory in some layouts) stores repository metadata, references, configuration and objects. Treat it as managed internal state and use Git commands instead of editing its files directly.
questions.explanation: The .git directory (or Git directory in some layouts) stores repository metadata, references, configuration and objects. Treat it as managed internal state and use Git commands instead of editing its files directly.

questions.prompt: Which command is the most direct starting point for this lesson’s example?
questions.explanation: Use `git rev-parse --git-dir` as the first inspection/action in the example, and then verify the result with the companion checks in the lesson.

questions.prompt: Which is the safest general practice when working with the .git directory?
options: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
Run the most destructive option first; the reflog guarantees every file can always be recovered.
Assume the local command also changed the remote and satisfied all hosting-platform policies.
questions.answer_key: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
questions.explanation: Inspect the repository state, verify the expected result, and protect valuable work before destructive or history-changing operations.
